The '''2003 World Championship''' was the 8th Star Wars CCG World Championship, run by the [[Players Committee]] at Dragon*Con in Atlanta, Georgia, over the convention's Labor Day weekend (29 August – 1 September 2003).<ref name="awards">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ Awards and Hall of Fame], starwarsccg.org; Wayback [https://web.archive.org/web/20230817222457/https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ 17 August 2023]</ref><ref name="dcon">[https://fancons.com/events/info/5400/dragon-con-2003 Dragon*Con 2003], FanCons.com (convention dates 29 August – 1 September 2003)</ref><ref name="pc-0905">[http://www.swccgpc.com/interior.htm SWCCGPC.com] (news of 5 September 2003: World Championship results, top 8 with deck pairs, Dragon*Con, Atlanta). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20031008101333/http://www.swccgpc.com/interior.htm Internet Archive]</ref> [[Jonny Chu]] defeated [[Greg Shaw]] in the final; the Players Committee's results give his decks as "Combat / Senate".<ref name="awards" /><ref name="pc-0905" /><ref name="tfn-2003" /> A third-place match was played, in which [[Clint Hays]] took 3rd over [[Bastian Winkelhaus]]; a forum poster recalls 2003 as the only year this was done.<ref name="pc-0905" /><ref name="f75427-1301004">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=1301004#p1301004 Post by allstarz97], "SWCCG Worlds Day 3 Standings History", forum.starwarsccg.org (3 June 2020). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261012152200/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t75427.html#p1301004 Internet Archive]</ref> The field size has not been found.

The Players Committee announced the venue on 23 March 2003, after players had learned that there would be no DecipherCon that year; the Young Jedi and Jedi Knights World Championships moved to Gen Con.<ref name="pc-mar03">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030819162615/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/Archives/march03archives.htm March Updates (2003): State Championship Info; World Championship Venues Announced! (23 March 2003)], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 19 August 2003.</ref> Dragon*Con 2003 was held in the Hyatt Regency Atlanta (265 Peachtree Street NE) and the Atlanta Marriott Marquis (265 Peachtree Center Ave).<ref name="pc-dragoncon03" /> The cash purse was $3,500, and the top 8 received glass trophies.<ref name="pc-wc03sched">[https://web.archive.org/web/20040620165803/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/Events/2003/worldchamps06122003.htm SWCCG World Championships Coming to Atlanta!], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 20 June 2004.</ref> After the event Decipher re-rated the World Championship with a "64K" value, which made Chu the new #1 ranked player.<ref name="pc-0905" />

The constructed pool was printed Decipher cards through [[Theed Palace]] plus the original [[Virtual Sets (2002-2009)|Players Committee Virtual Sets]] then legal. The wiki files it under [[Premiere - Original VS5]], from the newest virtual cards in the published lists. [[Virtual Set 5: A Dark Time|Virtual Set 5]] became tournament-legal on 6 June 2003,<ref name="pc-int0306">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030603182926/http://swccgpc.com:80/interior.htm SWCCGPC.com news: Virtual Set #5 Official Release! (30 May 2003)], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 3 June 2003.</ref> and the Committee did not release [[Virtual Set 6: City In The Clouds|Virtual Set 6]] until 21 November 2003,<ref name="pc-int0312">[https://web.archive.org/web/20031202154611/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/interior.htm SWCCGPC.com news (October–November 2003)], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 2 December 2003.</ref> so Virtual Set 5 was the newest set legal at Worlds. Rules Advocate [[Greg Anderson]]'s rules sheet of 23 August 2003 (final version 25 August) was the version used at Worlds.<ref name="pc-aug03">[https://web.archive.org/web/20040612215836/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/Archives/august03archives.htm August 03 Updates], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 12 June 2004.</ref>

=== Top 8 bracket ===

The quarterfinal and semifinal pairings and game results have not been found. The 3rd/4th place match (Hays def. Winkelhaus) is the only placement game recorded besides the final.<ref name="pc-0905" /><ref name="f75427-1301004" />

=== Schedule and prizes ===

The Players Committee's first schedule (June 2003) was:<ref name="pc-wc03sched" />

* Friday 29 August: 10 AM Day 1 qualifier in [[Classic]] format and 2 PM Day 1 qualifier in Open format, each six games of Swiss with the top 25% qualifying for Day 2. A player doing poorly in the first could drop and play the second.
* Saturday 30 August: 3 PM Day 2, eight games of Swiss, top 8 to Day 3.
* Sunday 31 August: 10 AM Day 3, single elimination with match play: each match was one Light and one Dark game against the same opponent, untimed.
* Monday 1 September: 12 PM award ceremony.

The Dragon*Con event page (August 2003) gave the final schedule: Day 1 Classic at 9 AM and Day 1 Open at 1 PM ($5 each; six games of Swiss, eight if more than 32 players; top 20% to Day 2, minimum 4; only for players without a Day 2 bye), Day 2 at 2 PM on Saturday (free; eight games of Swiss, top 8 to Day 3), Day 3 at 11 AM on Sunday ("Cash for Top 4") and the awards at 12 PM on Monday. In Day 3 the higher seed chose the first matchup, and "differential will be used in the case of split matches".<ref name="pc-dragoncon03" /> The final notice of 28 August added that every PC event carried a $2 charge paid to Dragon*Con, a Dragon*Con badge was required, decklists were required for Days 1, 2 and 3, and posted times were registration times, with play starting one hour later.<ref name="pc-aug03" />

The confirmed cash prizes were:<ref name="pc-wc03sched" />

== Side events ==

The Players Committee's Dragon*Con schedule listed these Star Wars CCG side events: a free Hoth Scenario constructed event and an EPP Overdrive Sealed Deck ($10) on Friday; Classic constructed ($5) and Episode 1 Sealed Deck ($10) on Saturday; Secret Squirrel Sealed Deck ($10), Episode 1 constructed ($5) and Highlander constructed ($5) on Sunday; and free Classic constructed and Secret Squirrel Sealed Deck events on Monday.<ref name="pc-dragoncon03" /> The PC also posted descriptions of these formats.<ref name="pc-formats03">[https://web.archive.org/web/20040617173044/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/Events/2003/formatdescriptions08282003.htm Format Descriptions for All Dragon*Con 2003 Events!], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 17 June 2004.</ref> A free OTSD Sealed Deck event at 12 PM on Sunday was offered to everyone who attended but did not qualify for Day 3, and "on the spot" 4-player tournaments could be run at any time.<ref name="pc-aug03" /> No side-event results have been found.
